subject: Price sculpting + deal packaging for Nebula AI (AWS/GCP private offers)
messages:
From: Jake Winters <jake.winters@nebula.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@nebula.ai>, procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Intro + target economics for pilot

Hi Olga / Camila,

Great conversation yesterday — thanks for the quick follow up. We want to move the pilot to a short private-offer engagement (AWS + GCP) but need to make sure the blended unit economics works for our procurement and channel partner (CloudBridge). High level asks from our side: 

- A single committed SKU for 6 months (node-hour equivalent) across AWS & GCP with a blended list price anchor.
- Partner (CloudBridge) margin carveout: they need a minimum 10% net to justify reselling/support.
- A small monthly retainer to cover operations and 24/7 tail support ($40k suggested).

Can you send a proposal that shows: (1) list price, (2) private-offer net after discounts, (3) partner pass-through margin, and (4) invoice routing options (direct vs marketplace invoice) so procurement can sign off quickly.

Also attaching a simple PO template (procurement wants the format).

Thanks,
Jake
--
Jake Winters
VP, Platform & ML Ops
Nebula AI
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Intro + target economics for pilot

Team — forwarding Nebula's asks. Quick assessment below, please weigh in: 

1) Blended SKU approach: we can create a private-offer on both AWS and GCP that share the same pricing table (private-offer alias) and a reconciliation clause. Works, but invoicing path matters for partner margin.

2) Partner margin: CloudBridge wants 10% net. We can offer a 12% gross commission inside the private offer and absorb tax / marketplace fees in the carry, but that reduces our net. Alternatively we keep 10% gross and offer a $40k monthly retainer to the partner. Need guidance on preferable structure.

3) Retainer: Nebula suggests $40k/mo; I'd prefer $50k with an operational SLA — gives us room to fund dedicated SRE support during pilot.

4) Procurement asks for PO format and DocuSign flow; Jordan, can you confirm whether a marketplace invoice (AWS) is acceptable as a contractual invoice for Nebula procurement?

Please review the attached draft proposal (Nebula_MA_proposal_v2.xlsx) and flag any redlines.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro + target economics for pilot

Olga / Camila — quick answers: 

- AWS marketplace invoices are generally acceptable for procurement, but some enterprise buyers insist on a Redwood-issued invoice (we can do either). For Nebula's PO process I recommend we offer both options and note that marketplace invoices will show AWS as the billing entity (impacts recognition).

- Partner margin / retainer structuring: if CloudBridge wants 10% net, we should structure as: 11% gross commission + $45k monthly retainer to the partner, with a performance clawback if usage < 50% of committed in months 1–3. That preserves our net while making partner economics predictable.

- Price sculpting option: propose a three-tier private offer:
  * Tier A (anchor): 60% of commit at list-anchor price (higher),
  * Tier B (mid): 30% at a modest discount,
  * Tier C (overflow): 10% at deeper discount but billed at marketplace overage rates.

This lets us keep higher realized ASP while giving procurement predictable spend bands.

Ben — I left a couple of margin scenarios in the attached sheet; can you run net revenue sensitivity (after commission + taxes + marketplace fees)?

-jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Deal Ops | Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro + target economics for pilot

Looping in my quick numbers — attached snapshot in the spreadsheet. Summary scenarios (all US region):

- Option 1 (10% partner gross, $40k retainer): Net to Redwood ~ 68% of list-anchor after marketplace fees and tax carry.
- Option 2 (11% partner gross, $45k retainer, 3-month under-utilization clawback): Net to Redwood ~ 72% of list-anchor.
- Option 3 (12% partner gross, $50k retainer, no clawback): Net to Redwood ~ 66% of list-anchor but partner very happy.

Recommendation: present Option 2 to Nebula as the preferred path (balanced economics + retainer). For the three-tier sculpting Jordan proposed, assumptions in the sheet model ASP uplift of ~8% vs straight blended discount.

I'll clean up the numbers and prepare a short one-pager to share with Nebula procurement.

-Ben
Ben Carter
Partner Finance | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Khatri <priya.khatri@nebula.ai>
To: Jake Winters <jake.winters@nebula.ai>, olga_petrov@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebula.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Price sculpting + deal packaging for Nebula AI (AWS/GCP private offers)

Hi all — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed numbers. We reviewed Option 2 internally and it looks promising. A few clarifying requests before procurement signs: 

- Can Redwood provide a one-page summary that maps the three-tier sculpting to the final PO line items (i.e., what to enter in our PO for Tier A/B/C quantities and prices)?
- For the partner retainer, we need the SOW language: what exactly CloudBridge is accountable for (response SLA, onboarding hours, escalation matrix).
- Please confirm how usage overage will be reported and charged when AWS invoices directly (we prefer a single combined monthly statement).

If you can get the one-pager + SOW bullet points + DocuSign-ready private-offer attachments by EOD Friday our procurement will prepare the PO and we can aim to start the pilot the week of Dec 13.

Best,
Priya
Priya Khatri
Head of Procurement
Nebula AI
